layers.root: Reserved for agentic-stack, the root contract every other skill assumes. It is the seventh layer in schemas/skill.schema.json and tools/validate_skills.py, it is not listed as a skill here, and it is exempt from the used_by symmetry check by design (ceremony 1 findings C1-004 and C1-001).
layers.core: The five owned components of PASS.md B2, Document, Planner, Graph, Judge and Ledger, each importing capability interfaces only and naming no product.
layers.cap: One skill per capability interface in PASS.md B3: it names the governing standard and version, defines the contract the core imports, ships two adapters whose execution models differ, and carries the caller's view itself - the -use facet was folded into the ideal on 2026-09-03. cap-consumption is the one cross-capability member of this layer: the consumption contract every capability shares, stated once.
layers.xc: One skill per cross-cutting concern in PASS.md B4, seven in total rather than grouped, because each has a distinct enforcement point, a distinct check, and a distinct way to fail open; the matching cap- skill defines the interface while the xc- skill defines the placement that a caller cannot decline, and merging the two is what produced conformance checks that exist outside the enforcement path (claimed, per PASS.md A6).
layers.seam: The two boundaries with no standard to adopt, Dispatch and State, where original design effort is warranted and where the platform's weight sits. seam-entry-envelope and seam-agent-ingress were dropped on 2026-09-03 and folded into cap-work-intake and cap-capability-registry, restoring this definition.
layers.compose: Assemblies of lower layers into a workflow, a bounded loop, a parked approval and an agent; a composition introduces no new interface. compose-workflow was merged into compose-operators on 2026-09-03, so the closed operator set is defined once and the sequence operator is a section of it.
layers.build: The disciplines every author in this repo uses regardless of layer: definition of done with a breakage, adapter pairing, evidence recording that keeps claimed and measured apart, and the skill authoring convention.

skills.name: seam-dispatch
skills.purpose: Execute one unit of agent work under a declared ceiling and return one typed result whose partial progress is already durable.
skills.standard: none published; assembled from A2A v1.0 task lifecycle (version unverified), Agent Client Protocol stop reasons (version unverified), RFC 9457, and draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header-07
skills.adapter_today: control-protocol dispatcher over vsock into a local microVM
skills.second_adapter: HTTP dispatcher into a hosted single-shot sandbox with no session and no callbacks
skills.notes_for_author: Folded (STATUS row 71): seam-dispatch-implement. Full design in decomposition.md section 2.1, including all four schema sketches. Do not invent a state machine or a stop-reason vocabulary: adopt the A2A task lifecycle and the ACP stop reasons and add only budget_exhausted, deadline_exceeded, policy_denied, cancel_timeout and adapter_unavailable. Three implementations exist today with no contract between them (claimed, per PASS.md B5); the conformance suite must be able to single out one failing adapter. Fold-in (research gaps dispatch-contract-that-is-explicit-about and context-contract-in-dispatch-the-request; X-cross-structure-042 through X-cross-structure-046, X-end-to-end-004 and X-end-to-end-005; T-t2-03 and T-t2-02; PASS.md B5): make durability explicit in the contract, every dispatch a recorded step with a step id, an idempotency key, a resumable checkpoint reference and a defined replay semantic where the recorded result is returned rather than the effect re-executed, satisfiable both by a durable engine and by a queue plus a state machine. Make context explicit too: the request declares what context the unit receives, the result declares the folded summary returned to the parent, and a compaction event is a first-class recorded transition rather than an invisible one. The adapter contrast to record is summarise-and-restart versus branch-and-fold into a fresh sub-agent context. The ideal facet also carries the usability section (how a human, an agent, and an event reach it; minimal inputs/outputs; failure shape) since this layer has no separate -use skill.

skills.purpose: Persist the graph and the ledger as one append-only tamper-evident log, written by one writer per run and read at a pinned snapshot.

skills.second_adapter: Merkle log over an object store with a fencing-lease writer and O(log n) proofs

Every planner query takes at_head and is deterministic at that head, which is what makes design rule 5 checkable. Redaction is a tombstone that preserves the record digest, never a deletion. Fold-in (research gap state-seam-specified-as-an-event-sourced, X-cross-structure-043, X-cross-structure-047, X-cross-structure-048, X-cross-structure-049, X-cross-structure-052, T-t2-03, PASS.md B5): specify the seam as an event-sourced append log, append(stream_id, expectedVersion, events) with a uniqueness constraint for conflict detection, periodic snapshots, named projections as the planner's query surface, and a Merkle inclusion-proof integrity mode alongside the hash chain, with file-plus-chain and a relational or object-store event log as the two adapters. skills.name: cap-work-intake
skills.purpose: Accept a job from any producer and turn it into one canonical document, whatever the producer was.
skills.standard: CloudEvents v1.0.2 (version unverified) and A2A protocol v1.0 (version unverified; specification text could not be fetched, domain egress-blocked)

skills.notes_for_author: Folded (STATUS row 71): cap-work-intake-implement. Idempotency and scheduling are apparent dependencies, not real ones: a schedule is one producer among several and the replay lease is applied above by xc-idempotency-lease. Whether both envelope formats stay first-class is open question 10. Fold-in (consolidation part A, 2026-09-03; kb/ceremonies/consolidation-review.json plan steps 7 and 8): the planned skill seam-entry-envelope and its -implement facet were dropped and their content belongs here. Its purpose was: Make every driving adapter produce one identical internal record, so nothing downstream ever branches on how the work arrived. Capability: Entry envelope. Standard: CloudEvents v1.0.2 core context attributes and HTTP protocol binding (version unverified). Adapter today: an HTTP driving adapter accepting a CloudEvent, plus the CLI adapter, both emitting the same envelope. Second adapter: a git-event or schedule adapter where no caller supplies ids, deriving the idempotency key as a fingerprint of selected payload elements, which breaks the assumption that the producer supplies the correlation and idempotency fields. Its definition of done: Identical work submitted through every entry adapter produces byte-identical envelopes apart from the source attribute and the minted run id, and an adapter that omits actor, ceiling or idempotency key is refused at the boundary instead of defaulted. Its notes were: Cite X-entry-composition-001, X-entry-composition-003, X-entry-composition-004, X-entry-composition-005 and X-entry-composition-015 for the envelope, X-cross-structure-016, X-cross-structure-017, X-cross-structure-018 and X-cross-structure-019 for the normalising mapping; target requirement T-t2-03; PASS.md B3. The envelope carries the CloudEvents required context attributes (id, source, specversion, type) plus actor and delegation chain, the correlation envelope, the budget ceiling and the idempotency key; every routing decision and every cross-cutting concern reads only this record. The platform mints its own run id and preserves the source protocol's ids as attributes rather than replacing them, so a caller can still find its own work. This is a seam and not a capability because no standard covers the mapping, only the envelope shape. Schedules and manual triggers are sibling entries producing this same envelope (folded into cap-scheduling), and the Document every adapter produces is core-document. Closes raw gaps entry-envelope-one-internal-record-every and an-intake-normaliser-one-required-mappin.
